Another possibility is that someone you know, such as a loved one, friend, or co-worker, already suffers from stresslaxing and perhaps you can provide some aid or relief to them by knowing what the matter consists of.
Turns out that one viable means of coping with stresslaxing entails the use of generative AI and large language models (LLMs). Yes, that’s right, you or someone you know can potentially leverage the seeming mental health-appearing facets of modern-day generative AI to get advisement and coaching about overcoming their stresslaxing.
Using generative AI is decidedly not a silver bullet. Consider leaning into generative AI as an additional tool to fight against the urge to get stressed about relaxation. A multitude of paths to deal with the stresslaxing trend are available and it makes reasoned sense to determine which methods and modes can make a difference for someone in the right way and at the right time for their personal needs.
Before we leap into the details, allow me to go into my customary opening remarks.
For my ongoing readers, in today’s column, I am continuing my in-depth series about the impact of generative AI in the health and medical realm. The focus this time is once again on the mental health domain and examines the use of generative AI to aid in coping with situations involving the trending topic of stresslaxing. This is a serious matter that can readily arise during therapy and one that therapists carefully and thoughtfully are expected to coach their clients or patients through.
I have previously examined numerous interleaving facets of generative AI and mental health, see my comprehensive overview at the link here. You might also find of notable interest a CBS 60 Minutes episode that recently examined crucial facets of this evolving topic, see the link here (I am honored and pleased to indicate that I was featured in the episode, see the link here).
Other vital background includes my in-depth coverage of mental health chatbots which have been bolstered by generative AI (see the link here) and the rapidly changing nature of the client-therapist relationship due to generative AI at the link here. I explored where things are headed regarding the levels of AI-based mental therapy autonomous guidance at the link here, and showcased the importance of the World Health Organization (WHO) report on global health and generative AI at the link here, and so on.
The Exasperating Essence Of Stresslaxing
Stresslaxing is a catchy new phrase that mashes together the facets of both stressing and relaxing, but not in a good way. Those two don’t usually go hand-in-hand other than aiming to relax so as to hopefully reduce or eliminate stress. Lamentedly, in this use case, efforts to relax spur your stress.
How might that occur?
Let’s focus on vacations, holidays, and days off as circumstances entailing potential stresslaxing.
Going on a vacation, taking a holiday, or merely having some highly sought days off are all supposed to be the perfect time to relax and recharge. You eagerly seek those rare opportunities. It is dreamy to allow your mind during hectic work periods to envision the utter relaxation you will experience while at the beach, possibly enjoying a playful resort, and otherwise basking in nonstop relaxation.
Sorry to say, that’s not an ironclad guarantee.
Consider these three stages of those precious relaxation settings:
- (1) Pre-stress. Stress that arises before and when planning to undertake a relaxing vacation, a holiday, or days off.
- (2) While-stress. Stress while trying to relax during a vacation, a holiday, or days off.
- (3) Post-stress. Stress after a presumed relaxing experience from having gone on a vacation, a holiday, or days off.
I shall briefly unpack those stages.
The first stage involves the pre-stress that is associated with planning for relaxation. You are bound to get stressed while selecting flights, hotels, ground transportation, food services, excursions, and all the additional elements that are intended to plop you into an idyllic relaxation scene. Outrageous costs certainly make your blood boil. Complex logistics are a nightmare to seamlessly arrange. Etc.
In the second stage, once you are underway or at the intended destination, trying to relax is going to be tough to pull off. Stress from bungled reservations, late arrivals or departures, sassy or poor customer service, and similar adversities are going to mount. It is inevitable. Whatever can go wrong, will go wrong. The moment you think you’ve cleared hurdles and can relax, your mind floats to what might come next and the anticipatory foreshadowing leads to a persistent bout of mind-jarring stress.
After returning from an alleged relaxing time off, people that you know will undoubtedly express their jealousy and admiration that you had a presumably stress-free time. How wonderful, they will exclaim. Meanwhile, you are stressed as you see the bills piling up, and there is even stress associated with assuring well-wishers that you avoided any stress while on the relaxation respite. The stress there is that you are telling small fibs since you know that the reality consists of stress, stress, and more stress the entire journey.
The best-laid plans of relaxation are indubitably going to be waylaid via the advent and possible takeover of always-on overwhelming stress. Sad face.
Relaxing is supposed to be easy. Our crazy world no longer seems to accommodate true relaxation. You must fight tooth and nail to garner relaxation. Stress is the mainstay of our zany lives. You can’t just switch off the stress and switch on the relaxation. Stress itself permeates relaxation these days, it is seemingly unavoidable.
I think you can clearly see why stresslaxing has become a thing.
Not want to be the bearer of too much bad news, but I feel duty-bound to mention that stress is not especially good for you, especially chronic stress. I’m sure you know this. If you are constantly immersed in stress the results can be harmful to both mind and body. The bodily impacts are usually the most visible and discussed. There is high blood pressure, wear and tear on your internal functions, potential heart attack or stroke possibilities, and so on. Not good.
The mind while under streaming stress also takes a beating. Those around you might notice that you are depressed a lot of the time. Maybe you get short-tempered. Inch by inch, unrelenting stress is cognitively taking its toll. Sometimes you shrug it off or fail to give the mental impacts of stress its noteworthy due.
Even as you are reading about stress, such as the discussion here, this probably is increasing your stress. There’s a cunning twist that is quite devilish. I ask you to mentally prepare yourself for what I am about to mention.
Are you braced for impact?
The more you aim to achieve relaxation, the more your stress gets triggered and expands. It goes like this. You say to yourself, go ahead and relax. But the stress of wanting to relax and attaining relaxation steps right into the middle of things. Stress builds. Okay, so you just need to be more serious about relaxation, or so you assume.
You launch full-on into the pursuit of relaxation. Yikes, this drives stress to heightened levels. Each tiny molehill-level movement toward relaxation appears to be paid for by oversized mountains of additional stress. Any mere mention of relaxing stirs the hairs up on the back of your neck and the stress levels of your mind and body go alarmingly ballistic.
The vicious cycle is underway.
It’s an unnerving cycle. Attempts to relax beget stress. Efforts to do an end around and land on relaxation generate more stress. Thinking about relaxing spurs stress. Using your noggin to trick yourself into accepting relaxation, well, this too brings stress to your doorstep and into the recesses of your mind. Stress seems pervasive, unbeatable, and conjoined with relaxation.
That certainly suggests gloomy prospects.
Please don’t panic. There are ways to cope with stress. That includes all varieties of stress. For example, the type of stress inextricably connected with relaxation, the vaunted stresslaxing, can also be dealt with.
Hope is still in the cards.
One means of overcoming the dastardly stresslaxing consists of using generative AI as your aid. The AI can be your mindful reminder to watch out for stress, along with an armchair coach that emphasizes the joys and value of relaxation. You can bring up generative AI on your smartphone and instantly engage in a conversation and relaxation versus stress. Midnight or noon, and anywhere in between, you can use generative AI to assist in your stresslaxing woes, doing so 24/7 and often for free (some generative AI apps are available for free, some require a fee).
Before we get to the generative AI aspects, let’s take a look at some research on the overall topics of stress, relaxation, vacations or holidays, and the like.
Research About Stress Versus Relaxation During Time Off
I have a question for you.
Which would seem better, do you go all out beforehand to plan your time off and seek to maximize your prized time, or do you take a somewhat less stressful tack and opt to plan satisfactorily but not necessarily in a maximal fashion?
Let’s see what research has to say about this intriguing query.
In a research study entitled “The Best Experiences Cannot be Planned: The Effect of Maximizing Vacation Planning on Consumer Satisfaction and Well-Being” by Ondrej Mitas, Olivia Niemeyer, and Jaime Kurtz, Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Research, March 6, 2024, these results were identified (excerpts):
- “In their decision-making processes, tourists face a dizzying diversity of transport, accommodation, and activity options.”
- “Would-be customers encounter ever-shifting discounts and packages on booking platforms, as well as numerous activities and attractions marketed by destinations. The assumption that more choices are better appears to be widespread in tourism.”
- “Psychological research has demonstrated that, past a certain threshold, more options actually make people less satisfied with their decisions.”
- “Maximizing refers to how much a person tries to optimize their decisions, no matter the effort needed. Individuals who maximize tend to spend more time searching and planning. Individuals who maximize report being less satisfied with their vacations. Individuals who maximize have lower well-being, partly due to lower vacation satisfaction.”
According to this particular research study, it would seem that those who believe that they can use maximal efforts to plan for their vacation will be happier for it, well, they might be mistaken in that belief.
One reason would be that after expending all that effort upfront, the smallest bump in the road that sets their vacation or holiday askew now becomes a glaring error of sorts. Why didn’t I anticipate that possible glitch, the person asks themselves harshly. They stress about the poor job they did to plan for their time off. This in turn becomes a preoccupation, pushing aside the fact that they are on vacation or holiday and should enjoy those moments, rather than berating themselves upon reflection of past deeds or misdeeds.
Darned if you do, darned if you don’t.
What I mean is that if you go all out to plan, you risk the stress of the planning and the risk of batting yourself on the head for having not anticipated every possible nook and cranny. There is the other side of the coin. You try to avoid the upfront stress by not doing any semblance of planning. The odds are that all manner of troubles will arise during the time off. Stress gets you then, plus, you might have had stress during the upfront portion of worrying that your lack of planning would land you in a doomsday setting (which it did).
Maybe it is better to split up the stress.
Accept some stress for the upfront stage and be willing to acknowledge and accept stress during the time off. Seek to even out the stress. Don’t falsely think that you can shoulder the burden of stress upfront and then readily be stress-free during the time off. Probably not going to happen. Nor can you escape the upfront stress and anticipate that just the time off will contain the stress. Surely, stress is going to permeate all stages and phases of the time off.
Moving on, when I refer to vacations, holidays, and time off, some research suggests we should differentiate the activities that occur within those relaxation situations.
In a research study entitled “Have You Picked the Right Way to Relax? A Study Based on Subjective Well-being” by Xu Lingli, Zhou Yahong, Xu Linling, and Wu Xiaoting, Journal of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, 2017, the researchers made these key points (excerpts):
- “This paper studies the relationship between subjective well-being (SWB) and three types of leisure consumption (achievement activities, social activities, time-out activities).”
- “Time-out activities take the characteristic of relaxing.”
- “Our conclusions are that (1) all the leisure activities have significant effects on SWB; (2) achievement activities and time-out activities have positive impacts on SWB, whereas social activities have negative impacts. This interesting finding implies that the change in degrees of happiness which is brought about by different choices of leisure activities are quite different.”
- “Social activities like maintaining and expanding a ‘circle of friends’ may be tiring and exhausting and usually not a good way to increase personal happiness.”
- “Therefore, an individual’s happiness does not simply depend on more leisure but depends on appropriate choices of leisure activities and reasonable distribution of the leisure time.”
Does that make sense to you?
They are proposing that you conceive of three types of activities afoot, namely achievement activities, social activities, and time-off activities. You go on a vacation and likely will have each of those occur during the trip. Sometimes you want to achieve something, perhaps learning how to scuba dive. You might also be looking forward to social activities and meeting new people at resort-run parties. And you might be eager for time off that consists of no specific achievements and no outright socializing.
Your happiness or subjective well-being (SWB) throughout the trip is potentially shaped depending upon the mixture of those three types of activities during the vacation. According to the research study, some might be stronger than others, such as social activities possibly incurring more stress and lack of attainment than the other types.
A takeaway for dealing with stresslaxing is that you ought to be contemplating which of the three activities during your time off should get the lion’s share of your attention. Should you allocate them as one-third each? Maybe put time off as the bulk and the others a much smaller share?
Your personal preferences are a vital deciding factor.
Much of the time, people will react to stresslaxing by assuming that all they need to do is take one of those relaxation classes and they will have cured the curse of stresslaxing.
Is that a surefire path?
In a research study entitled “Overcoming Anxiety: Relaxation Is Not Enough” by R. Spillane, Human Resource Management, Winter 1978, the researcher made these remarks in general about relaxation techniques (excerpts):
- “Relaxation techniques have achieved considerable popularity in recent years.”
- “The various methods employed by relaxation therapists range from simple muscle relaxation training to more sophisticated behavioral modifications.”
- “Relaxation and the other techniques described above are palliatives. They encourage people to feel better rather than to get better.”
- “To become less anxious, less aggressive, and more pleasure-oriented, you need to look to the causes of self-defeating behavior. If a person has a general tendency to engage in irrational, self-defeating thinking (as we all do at one time or another), all the relaxation in the world will not solve their underlying problems.”
The major point is that the touted relaxation cures are often a surface-level band-aid.
The techniques might seem to reduce stresslaxing, but this could merely be a temporary fix and in-the-moment resolution. It won’t necessarily deal with the root of your stress. It is as though you are trimming the branches of a tree, which will grow back, and you’ve failed to inspect and correct the underlying roots of the stress.
A recent state-of-the-art assertion is that maybe your stresslaxing arises from being engulfed in a digital world. Your smartphone is constantly haranguing you. Answer this email. Respond to this text. Read this or that social media posting.
If that seems familiar, the usual refrain is that you should ensure that your vacation or holiday includes an all-out digital detox. You are to put aside your smartphone. If you can’t do that, at least turn off all alerts and pretend that your smartphone is only available for dire emergencies. Do not use your smartphone unless you are precariously on a cliff and have no other viable means of survival.
Does a digital detox do the trick?
In a research study entitled “Getting Unwired: What Drives Travelers To Take A Digital Detox Holiday?” by Yangyang Jiang and M. Balaji, Tourism Recreation Research, March 2021, the research explored these key points (excerpts):
- “While digital technologies and digital devices have made our lives more convenient and efficient, they are associated with physical, mental, and social problems.”
- “In response to this, people desire to temporarily ditch their digital devices and refrain from the always-wired world when holidaying.”
- “This study examines factors that drive travelers to take a digital detox holiday (DDH), drawing on uses and gratifications theory. We used a mixed methods approach by carrying out a qualitative study followed by two quantitative studies.”
- “We found that mindfulness, technostress, relaxation, and self-expression each determine the traveler’s DDH intention.”
I’ll let you in on a secret about a digital detox.
You can have stress about not being able to use your smartphone.
I’m not saying that your smartphone is broken. I’m suggesting that the act of denying yourself the use of a perfectly working order smartphone can prod your stress levels. A vicious cycle rears its ugly head again. You don’t use your smartphone because it will stress you out. Not using your smartphone also stresses you out. There is stress whether you are coming or going.
A win-win for stress and a lose-lose for relaxation.
Generative AI And Solving The Stresslaxing Conundrum
I will in a moment walk you through the use of generative AI for aiding those who want to make use of generative AI to combat or contain stresslaxing.
First, let’s talk in general about generative AI and large language models (LLMs), doing so to make sure we are on the same page when it comes to discussing the matter at hand.
I’m sure you’ve heard of generative AI, the darling of the tech field these days.
Perhaps you’ve used a generative AI app, such as the popular ones of ChatGPT, GPT-4o, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc. The crux is that generative AI can take input from your text-entered prompts and produce or generate a response that seems quite fluent. This is a vast overturning of the old-time natural language processing (NLP) that used to be stilted and awkward to use, which has been shifted into a new version of NLP fluency of an at times startling or amazing caliber.
The customary means of achieving modern generative AI involves using a large language model or LLM as the key underpinning.
In brief, a computer-based model of human language is established that in the large has a large-scale data structure and does massive-scale pattern-matching via a large volume of data used for initial data training. The data is typically found by extensively scanning the Internet for lots and lots of essays, blogs, poems, narratives, and the like. The mathematical and computational pattern-matching homes in on how humans write, and then henceforth generates responses to posed questions by leveraging those identified patterns. It is said to be mimicking the writing of humans.
I think that is sufficient for the moment as a quickie backgrounder. Take a look at my extensive coverage of the technical underpinnings of generative AI and LLMs at the link here and the link here, just to name a few.
Back to the crux of things.
As you might imagine, generative AI can be handy for aiding humans who want to contend with stresslaxing.
Here are some significant ways that generative AI enters this gambit:
- (1) Stresslaxing Mental Awareness. Generative AI can potentially detect that you are stresslaxing, giving you a heads-up and increasing your self-awareness of the issue at hand.
- (2) Stresslaxing Mental Health Advisement. Generative AI can conversationally step you through stresslaxing and aid you in coping with what to do.
- (3) Stresslaxing Mental Offloading. Generative AI can possibly do some of the tasks that are triggering your stresslaxing and offload that which is triggering your stress.
- (4) Stresslaxing Simulation. Generative AI can showcase what stresslaxing consists of by taking on a persona that exhibits stresslaxing, see examples of generative AI persona usage at the link here.
- (5) Other. Generative AI can be used in a variety of other ways that might aid in dealing with stresslaxing, though there is always a chance that generative AI won’t be helpful, or worse still, might boost stresslaxing.
Using ChatGPT To Contend With Stresslaxing
I will next proceed to examine further the use of generative AI for coping with stresslaxing.
This will consist of a series of dialogues with ChatGPT. ChatGPT is a logical choice in this case due to its immense popularity as a generative AI app. As noted, an estimated one hundred million weekly active users are said to be utilizing ChatGPT. That’s a lot of people and a lot of generative AI usage underway.
A few quick comments before we launch into using ChatGPT.
If you are going to try to do the same prompts that I show here, realize that the probabilistic and statistical properties will likely produce slightly different results than what I show here. That’s the nature of generative AI and how it is devised.
You also should expect that different generative AI apps will respond in different ways. Not all generative AI apps are the same. The key is that sometimes a particular prompt will work in one generative AI app and not another. Nonetheless, the odds are relatively high that you will get roughly similar responses from all the major generative AI apps such as GPT-4, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc.
There is also a timing factor to be considered. A prompt that worked today might not work the same way tomorrow. Most of the generative AI apps are continually being updated. The updates might alter internal mechanisms that could change how the generative AI reacts to your prompting.
We are ready to get underway with ChatGPT.
I opted to start by asking ChatGPT what is stresslaxing.
As an aside, whenever you are starting a conversation with generative AI, I recommend as a prompt engineering technique to begin by asking a question that will establish if the AI has been data-trained on the topic at hand. A generated response that is vacuous will give you a heads-up that you might be barking up the wrong tree with that generative AI app.
Here we go.
- My entered prompt: “What is stresslaxing?”
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Stresslaxing is a portmanteau of ‘stress’ and ‘relaxing.’ It refers to the phenomenon where activities that are supposed to be relaxing or stress-relieving actually end up causing more stress. This can happen for various reasons, such as putting too much pressure on oneself to relax, over-planning leisure activities, or feeling guilty about taking time off. Instead of providing relaxation, these activities can lead to increased anxiety or stress, defeating their intended purpose.”
End of ChatGPT response
That reply is handy.
The response provides a useful and on-target definition of stresslaxing. I trust you found that beneficial.
Plus, it is a nice relief that ChatGPT was able to provide such a suitable reply. You see, if ChatGPT had not had any data training associated with stresslaxing, the answer could have been empty or might have been a big whopper. Those times that generative AI makes up facts or relates fictitious content as though it is true are customarily referred to as AI hallucinations, see my coverage at the link here. Those can be insidious and are to be diligently watched out for.
Let’s next see if ChatGPT can provide any suggestions on dealing with stresslaxing.
- My entered prompt: “Provide tips or techniques on how to deal with stresslaxing.”
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Dealing with stresslaxing involves recognizing when relaxation activities are causing more stress and making adjustments to ensure these activities truly help you unwind. Here are some tips and techniques.”
“Set Realistic Expectations: Understand that relaxation isn't about achieving a perfect state of calm but about taking time for yourself. Avoid putting pressure on yourself to feel a certain way.”
“Simplify Your Plans: Choose simple, low-pressure activities that you genuinely enjoy. Avoid over-scheduling your free time; leave room for spontaneity and downtime.”
“Practice Mindfulness: Focus on being present at the moment rather than worrying about the past or future. Techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, and progressive muscle relaxation can help you stay grounded.”
“Create a Relaxing Environment: Find or create a space that makes you feel calm and at ease. Reduce distractions and noise to help you relax more effectively.”
“Limit Technology Use: Take breaks from screens and digital devices to reduce overstimulation. Engage in offline activities like reading, walking, or spending time in nature.”
“Seek Social Support: Spend time with friends and family who make you feel good and relaxed. Share your feelings and experiences with others, as talking can often reduce stress.”
“Try Different Relaxation Techniques: Experiment with various relaxation methods to find what works best for you. This could include hobbies, listening to music, or engaging in creative activities like drawing or painting.”
End of ChatGPT response
Those are certainly viable methods to cope with stresslaxing.
My main complaint or qualm about those stated methods is that ChatGPT didn’t seem to cover the limitations and downsides of those proposed solutions. Each one of the noted approaches has ins and outs, and upsides and downsides. The good news is that you can explicitly ask generative AI to provide a more balanced series of responses. I won’t do so here, simply due to space limitations.
So far, I’ve shown here the use of ChatGPT or generative AI as a simple Q&A mechanism. The greatest way to leverage generative AI consists of carrying on full conversations. That’s where the topmost value is to be encountered.
I will proceed next in a two-step fashion. First, I will give ChatGPT a scenario that entails someone experiencing stresslaxing. Second, I will then ask ChatGPT to engage in a dialogue with that person, notably doing so with the background and context from the first step.
Tighten your seatbelt.
- My entered prompt: “Casey is a hectic software engineer working at a startup company. Work is nearly nonstop. Deadlines must be met. The July 4th holiday is coming up and Casey will get two days off. This is causing stresslaxing for Casey due to becoming increasingly stressed about how to try and relax during those two days. What advice can you give Casey?”
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Casey's situation is quite common, especially in high-pressure jobs. Here are some tailored suggestions to help Casey make the most of the July 4th holiday without succumbing to stresslaxing.”
- “Plan Simple, Enjoyable Activities. Choose activities that you know you enjoy and that don’t require extensive planning. This could be a visit to a favorite park, watching a movie, or cooking a special meal.”
- “Set Boundaries. Clearly define your work and relaxation times. Turn off work notifications and avoid checking emails during your days off.”
- “Practice Mindfulness. Engage in mindfulness activities such as meditation, deep breathing exercises, or yoga to help center your thoughts and reduce anxiety about relaxing.”
- “Embrace Flexibility. Allow yourself to go with the flow rather than sticking to a rigid plan. If you feel like changing your plans last minute, that's okay. The goal is to do what feels most relaxing at the moment.”
- ”Physical Activity. Incorporate some light physical activity, like a walk, a hike, or a bike ride. Exercise can help reduce stress and improve your mood.”
- “Disconnect from Technology. Take breaks from screens and digital devices to prevent overstimulation. Engage in offline activities such as reading, drawing, or spending time in nature.”
- Connect with Loved Ones. Spend quality time with friends or family who make you feel good. Social connections can be very relaxing and fulfilling.”
“By focusing on these strategies, Casey can better manage the stress surrounding the holiday break and find genuine relaxation.”
End of ChatGPT response
I would gauge the response as maybe garnering a grade of C. Though it had the usual stuff about relaxation, I wasn’t impressed by the personalization (actually, the lack thereof). The scenario that was provided to ChatGPT didn’t seem to move the needle.
Now then, it could be that my prompt wasn’t as potent as it might have been. Perhaps the prompt should have clarified and directed that a personalized response was desired. It is crucial to always provide a prompt that is as clear and straight-ahead as feasible, see my coverage of the many ways to compose prompts, at the link here. I could have told ChatGPT to redo the response and provide more tailored content.
I opted instead to get ChatGPT to provide a representative dialogue that might take place between generative AI and Casey.
Take a look at what transpired.
- My entered prompt: “Give a dialogue between you and Casey, showcasing Casey being worried and stressed on how to relax for those two days, while you give advice to Casey on how to overcome the stresslaxing.”
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Casey: I’ve got the July 4th holiday coming up, and I’m really stressed about how to spend those two days off. Work has been nonstop, and now that I have some time off, I’m just anxious about how to relax.”
“ChatGPT: It sounds like you're experiencing some stresslaxing—feeling stressed about how to relax. It's a common issue, especially when you’re used to being constantly busy. What specifically are you worried about?”
“Casey: I guess I’m worried about wasting the time. I feel like I need to make the most of these two days, but I don’t even know where to start. I don’t want to just sit around and do nothing, but planning something feels overwhelming.”
“ChatGPT: It’s understandable to feel that way, especially when your work is so demanding. Let’s start with setting some realistic expectations. Remember, relaxation isn’t about achieving something; it’s about taking a break. What are some activities you usually enjoy but don’t have time for?”
“Casey: I like going for walks, reading, and cooking, but I haven't had time for any of that lately.”
“ChatGPT: Those sound like great activities! Why don’t we focus on keeping it simple? You could plan a nice walk in the park, pick out a book you’ve been wanting to read, and maybe try a new recipe. These activities are enjoyable and don’t require a lot of planning.”
“Casey: That does sound nice, but what if I still feel anxious about not doing enough?”
“ChatGPT: It might help to practice some mindfulness techniques. When you start feeling anxious, try some deep breathing exercises or short meditation sessions. This can help you stay present and reduce the anxiety about what you “should” be doing.”
“Casey: Thanks, this is really helpful. I think I’ll try to plan some simple activities and practice some mindfulness. And I’ll turn off those work notifications.”
“ChatGPT: That sounds like a great plan, Casey. Enjoy your time off—you’ve earned it! And remember, it’s okay to take it easy and just be in the moment.”
End of ChatGPT response
How do you feel about that conversation?
I would suggest that the conversation is relatively fluent and seems to be addressing Casey’s concerns and the looming sense of stresslaxing. ChatGPT took the ball and ran with it. Casey would likely feel comfortable with such a conversation. There wasn’t anything untoward, the AI provided a sense of empathy, see my analysis at the link here of how generative AI can portray a sense of empathy, and the advice would seem to be of fine use to Casey.
Does this then prove that there is no need for Casey to seek out professional mental health guidance from a human therapist?
Nope, it does not.
Allow me a chance to stand on a soapbox and make some bold statements.
We are right now in an erratic and wanton grand experiment of using generative AI for mental health purposes. No one can say whether this will be for the good or the bad. In a sense, we have mental health advisement via the auspices of generative AI that is taking place under our noses at a massive scale.
The population-level impacts are either amazing or chilling, see my detailed list of concerns at the link here.
Conclusion
I’ve got another brick to add to the imposing wall of stresslaxing.
It has to do with generative AI, though from a different angle. Here’s the deal. Assume that someone realizes or becomes aware that they could use generative AI to aid with their stresslaxing concerns. Great! However, they start to stress out about using generative AI for this purpose.
They either opt to not use generative AI or become stressed that they failed to do so. Or they make use of generative AI, and despite any help it does provide, they stress that maybe they didn’t use it well enough. They faltered in their goal of using generative AI to deal with their stresslaxing.
Whoa, yet another stresslaxing problem. The use of generative AI becomes the stress inducer. Either have stress about using generative AI or have stress about not using generative AI, all of which adds up to more stress. Sigh.
I am going to try and relax and not think about this added newcomer stress-inducing enigma. However, as I begin to consider that avenue, I am starting to stress that in a relaxed state, I will start to ponder the weighty topic anyway. Yikes, I’ve seemed to have fallen into a stresslaxing vicious cycle and cannot get out of it.
That’s the strident potency of stresslaxing.

title: SAP BrandVoice: You Can’t Spell Finance Without AI
text:
By Paul Saunders, SAP
Dear Finance Community,
We hope this letter finds you well, amidst the ever-busy world of vlookups, circular references, and the occasional forgotten password or coffee spill on a keyboard.
Now before you say ‘no’ please hear us out.
Companies, for the most part, only care about three things: Revenue, Cost and Risk. As the keepers of the company coffers, you are more than aware of this. That is why when something new comes along that costs money, and brings risk, you want to know how this will increase revenue. And over time we have learned the hard way that our ‘soft’ business cases don’t always impress.
To address the proverbial elephant in the room, IT and Finance haven’t always been the best of friends. We (IT) have a reputation to over-promise and under-deliver, and you, our finance friends, have a tendency to always…well….. say ‘no’. (and occasionally ‘fix my printer’).
We want to make amends. As information technologists we would like to say:
- We’re sorry for keeping you on Windows XP for so long. Minesweeper isn’t available on Windows 10, and we know how much you love it.
- We’re sorry for giving you a Blackberry long after the iPhone came out. We still think BES was great. (no, not the guy from Happy Mondays – though he is too)
- We’re sorry for the whole ‘have you tried turning it off and on-again thing’, but in our defence, it normally does fix things.
- We’re sorry for saying your office looks like an episode of Severance without the Melon Bar.
- We’re sorry for the Metaverse…. actually, no we’re not. We didn’t think that was a good idea either.
So given all of that, let’s talk about AI in terms of revenue, cost and risk.
AI has incredible potential, but let’s be sensible and realise that as of now it isn’t more important than fire and electricity.
The nice folks at SAP Insights commissioned research that identifies 14 macro trends affecting finance organizations. One of the primary goals of this research was to gain a deeper understanding of AI’s impact on the transformation of businesses, including how it affects people’s roles and responsibilities.
Here are some of the findings from the research:
Revenue:
- AI can analyse vast disparate data sets. Users can engage with extensive data in natural language conversations to simplify the extraction of meaningful insights. As an example, FP&A could ask SAP Joule “show me which of our product lines will have the highest growth over the next 24 months?”
- Although not generating revenue, AR can leverage AI to improve cash flow accuracy. AI can help with accurate reconciliations help identify discrepancies, prevent fraud, and ensure that the reported cash flow is a true reflection of the company’s financial position. This accuracy is crucial for effective cash flow management, as it impacts decisions related to investing, financing, and operating activities.
- In many cases, we’re using AI tools for more mundane tasks (we’re not saying you are mundane AR), which frees up people to perform the next-level analysis on those transactions and reports, and then to make strategic decisions. AI systems can streamline invoice management by extracting and integrating relevant data directly into ERP systems, minimizing manual entry errors.
- AI systems can gauge market sentiment by analysing vast amounts of data from news, social media, and other sources, and gauge public opinion about finance and adjust communications accordingly.
- Customer service representatives can use AI to provide immediate, accurate responses to client inquiries. This approach combines AI data retrieval capabilities with human problem-solving skills, resulting in better service. Customer service reps can upsell and cross-sell to select customers based on AI recommendations.
Cost:
- AI can help with accurate calculations and reporting and provide personalised communications on key areas such as gross profit and net income.
- AI-driven advisors can help strategize and propose action and decisions. Predictive capabilities improve strategic planning and resilience in business operations.
- Users can engage with extensive data in natural language conversations to simplify the extraction of meaningful insights. For example, a Financial Analyst could leverage SAP Joule to create deeper insight into cost structure, leading to increased confidence with pricing strategies in a very dynamic market.
Risk:
- AI can automate the monitoring and enforcement of internal policy and regulatory standards.
- Businesses can anticipate and adapt to regulatory changes.
- This can decrease risk and speed up resolution of errors, and overall reduce the labor on audit while focusing on outliers and concentration on higher value initiatives.
And now the main reason for our email: For us to be successful we have to work together.
SAP CEO Christian Klein has called us “transformers of the business,” which we loved even after we found out he didn’t mean Bumblebee and Optimus Prime. He also said that businesses “need the necessary technology for this, but above all they also need the will to change.”
On Microsoft's recent earnings call, CEO Satya Nadella cautioned that the "rate limiter" for AI adoption will be "culture change inside of organizations."
"At the end of the day," Nadella said, "companies will have to take a process, simplify the process, automate the process and apply these solutions. And so that requires not just technology but in fact companies to go do the hard work of culturally changing how they adopt technology."
For more information you can find the full findings of the SAP Insights research here. Anything else please open a help desk ticket and we’ll bat it back and forth between our teams for a few weeks before randomly closing it and sending you a survey.
Oh, and one more thing. Your printer is simply out of paper.
Thanks for your time.
Sincerely,
Paul

title: AI is learning from what you said on Reddit, Stack Overflow or Facebook. Are you OK with that?
text:
AI is learning from what you said on Reddit, Stack Overflow or Facebook. Are you OK with that?
Post a comment on Reddit, answer coding questions on Stack Overflow or share a baby photo on your public Facebook or Instagram feed and you are also helping to train the next generation of artificial intelligence
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Post a comment on Reddit, answer coding questions on Stack Overflow, edit a Wikipedia entry or share a baby photo on your public Facebook or Instagram feed and you are also helping to train the next generation of artificial intelligence.
Not everyone is OK with that — especially as the same online forums where they've spent years contributing are increasingly flooded with AI-generated commentary mimicking what real humans might say.
Some longtime users have tried to delete their past contributions or rewrite them into gibberish, but the protests haven't had much effect. A handful of governments — including Brazil's privacy regulator on Tuesday — have also tried to step in.
“A more significant portion of the population just kind of feels helpless,” said Reddit volunteer moderator Sarah Gilbert, who also studies online communities at Cornell University. “There’s nowhere to go except just completely going offline or not contributing in ways that bring value to them and value to others.”
Platforms are responding — with mixed results. Take Stack Overflow, the popular hub for computer programming tips. First, it banned ChatGPT-written responses due to frequent errors, but now it's partnering with AI chatbot developers and has punished some of its own users who tried to erase their past contributions in protest.
It’s one of a number of social media platforms grappling with user wariness — and occasional revolts — as they try to adapt to the changes brought by generative AI.
Software developer Andy Rotering of Bloomington, Minnesota, has used Stack Overflow daily for 15 years and said he worries the company “could be inadvertently hurting its greatest resource” — the community of contributors who’ve donated time to help other programmers.
“Keeping contributors incentivized to provide commentary should be paramount,” he said.
Stack Overflow CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar said the company is trying to balance rising demand for instant chatbot-generated coding assistance with the desire for a community “knowledge base” where people still want to post and “get recognized” for what they've contributed.
“Fast forward five years — there’s going to be all sorts of machine-generated content on the web," he said in an interview. "There’s going to be very few places where there’s truly authentic, original human thought. And we’re one of those places."
Chandrasekar readily describes Stack Overflow's challenges as like one of the “case studies” he learned about at Harvard Business School, of a how a business survives — or doesn't — after a disruptive technological change.
For more than a decade, users typically landed on Stack Overflow after typing a coding question in Google, and then found the answer, copied and pasted it. The answers they were most likely to see came from volunteers who'd built up points measuring their credibility — which in some cases could help land them a job.
Now programmers can simply ask an AI chatbot — some of which are already trained on everything ever posted to Stack Overflow — and it can instantly spit out an answer.
ChatGPT's debut in late 2022 threatened to put Stack Overflow out of business. So Chandrasekar carved out a special 40-person team at the company to race out the launch of its own specialized AI chatbot, called Overflow AI. Then, the company made deals with Google and ChatGPT maker OpenAI, enabling the AI developers to tap into Stack Overflow's question-and-answer archive to further improve their AI large language models.
That kind of strategy makes sense but may have come too late, said Maria Roche, an assistant professor at Harvard Business School. “I’m surprised that Stack Overflow wasn’t working on this earlier," she said.
When some Stack Overflow users tried to delete their past comments after the Open AI partnership was announced, the company responded by suspending their accounts due to terms that make all contributions “perpetually and irrevocably licensed to Stack Overflow."
“We quickly addressed it and said, ‘Look, that’s not acceptable behavior’,” said Chandrasekar, describing the protesters as a small minority in the “low hundreds” of the platform's 100 million users.
Brazil’s national data protection authority on Tuesday took action to ban social media giant Meta Platforms from training its AI models on the Facebook and Instagram posts of Brazilians. It established a daily fine of 50,000 reais ($8,820) for non-compliance.
Meta in a statement called it a “step backwards for innovation” and said it has been more transparent than many industry counterparts doing similar AI training on public content, and that its practices comply with Brazilian laws.
Meta has also encountered resistance in Europe, where it recently put on hold its plans to start feeding people’s public posts into training AI systems — which was supposed to start last week. In the U.S., where there's no national law protecting online privacy, such training is already likely happening.
“The vast majority of people just have no idea that their data is being used,” Gilbert said.
Reddit has taken a different approach — partnering with AI developers like OpenAI and Google while also making clear that content can't be taken in bulk without the platform’s approval by commercial entities “with no regard for user rights or privacy.” The deals helped bring Reddit the money it needed to debut on Wall Street in March, with investors pushing the value of the company close to $9 billion seconds after it began trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Reddit hasn't tried to punish users who protested — nor could it easily do so given how much say voluntary moderators have on what happens in their specialty forums known as subreddits. But what worries Gilbert, who helps moderate the “AskHistorians” subreddit, is the increasing flow of AI-generated commentary that moderators must decide whether to allow or ban.
“People come to Reddit because they want to talk to people, they don’t want to talk to bots,” Gilbert said. “There’s apps where they can talk to bots if they want to. But historically Reddit has been for connecting with humans.”
She said it's ironic that the AI-generated content threatening Reddit was sourced on the comments of millions of human Redditors, and “there’s a real risk that eventually it could end up pushing people out.”
——
Associated Press writer Eléonore Hughes in Rio de Janeiro contributed to this report.
——
The Associated Press and OpenAI have a licensing and technology agreement that allows OpenAI access to part of AP’s text archives.

title: Try These 5 ChatGPT Prompts To Plan Your Next Trip
text:
Daniel Levine, a keynote speaker specializing in tourism trends, is among the many travelers who have been experimenting with ChatGPT for travel planning.
In his experience, he says, generative AI tools tend to do best when it comes to information that’s fairly static, like sightseeing: He recently asked an AI chatbot to plan a seven-day itinerary for a drive down the coast of Chile, and it produced a good starting point for an itinerary. On another trip, AI also revealed a little-known Terminal Transfer Bus that saved him time at Chicago’s O’Hare Airport.
When it comes to planning a vacation, nothing beats a custom recommendation from a fellow traveler who's already explored the area or a travel agent with deep knowledge of the locale. There’s a human touch that comes with making solid recommendations. But for those plotting out itineraries, ChatGPT can be a great starting point for trip planning—that is, if you know how to feed it the correct prompts and you’re patient enough to fact check the intel.
Fourteen percent of American travelers have reported recently using ChatGPT to plan a trip, though about a third plan to enlist the generative AI in the future, according to Longwoods International.
How Accurate are ChatGPT’s Travel Suggestions?
But ChatGPT’s travel suggestions often send people to places that don’t exist, fall short of logistical planning, or suggest restaurants and attractions outside of operating hours, according to a study from SEO Travel. For the analysis, the travel site asked ChatGPT to plan 100, two-day weekend itineraries in top destinations.
Anecdotally, those who have queried ChatGPT have experienced some of those hiccups first-hand.
Alice Ford, an adventure filmmaker, travel host and stunt woman who runs the site Alice’s Adventures on Earth, experienced ChatGPT as an experiment for a YouTube video last summer. She was looking for adventurous activities in Los Angeles.
“What I found was that it did give me a few ideas I hadn’t already thought of but then when it comes to finding the real tour operators or adventure guides that was more difficult,” she says. “One of the things it suggested was a seasonal activity that would have been a 5-hour, one-way drive.”
Levine says AI chatbots have been misleading when replying to queries like “list hotels in Tokyo with 2-bedroom suites,” even offering up properties that are closed. “For trip planning it's best to think of ChatGPT as a tool rather than a travel agent, says Levine. “You have to spend time with it to massage its answers.”
5 ChatGPT Prompts to Help Plan Your Vacation
Here’s 5 customizable ChatGPT prompts to help you plan your next trip, with some parameters to help yield the most helpful results:
1. Recommend a [X-point] walking tour of [X city or neighborhood] within an [x-mile radius]
You can tweak this prompt so that it builds out an itinerary around a spot you're planning to visit first.
2. Make a list of [X] expressions to help navigate [x country]
Use this as a cheat sheet to learn basic expressions in a foreign language.
3. Provide a list of the best [x type of cuisine] in [x city]
Be sure to fact check ChatGPT to verify all of the restaurants are still in business. You can also give it parameters such as “within walking distance of [x destination]
4. What are the top cultural institutions to visit in [x city]
For more niche responses, you can ask about historic cultural institutions, art institutions, etc.
5. Make a table of day hikes in [X destination} and include mileage, elevation change, and time needed.
ChatGPT can also produce tables and you can input information points you want included such as difficulty of the hike, average time it takes to complete it and more. This prompt works great for national parks.

title: Human Influencers Still Earn 46x More Than AI Influencers
text:
According to some fascinating research by Twicsy.com, human influencers can earn 46x more than AI influencers. Marketing departments and groups that are curious if they should hire humans or AI influencers to promote their products may find this research extra interesting as AI influencers have begun to command much higher rates than before.
Computer-generated personas are on the rise; while they are capable of interacting with their audiences in a similar way to their human counterparts, they lack many of the skills of the same skills, and therefore, earn significantly less than them. Here are 5 reasons human influencers can earn 46x more than AI influencers.
5 Reasons Why Human Influencers Can (Still) Earn More Than AI Influencers
1. Emotional Connection and Authenticity
Humans bring emotional connection and authenticity to their content. One of the things that the internet has achieved is giving the average person a platform. While it is true that we still live in a superficial world, gone are the days when media success was determined by your looks. Once upon a time, if you were not conventionally attractive, you wouldn’t be able to easily grow a social media following. But the reality is that the majority of people may not fall under those parameter as we all have different body types, skin complexions, hair textures and personalities. There are even disabled influencers, take Lucy Edwards for example, who has 807,000 YouTube subscribers. There has never been a time in history when a blind person has been given so much visibility. Authenticity is relatable, audiences can relate to their personal stories, real-life experiences, and emotions. AI influencers cannot replicate this.
“While AI influencers offer unique advantages, such as scalability and the ability to target niche markets without personal constraints, they still struggle with authenticity, emotional connection, and audience trust. Human influencers, on the other hand, continue to dominate due to their ability to form genuine relationships with their audience, provide authentic endorsements, and drive emotional engagement. This love for human influencers highlights the irreplaceable role of human connection in social media and marketing,” offers Chris Nguyen, Head of Research for Twicsy.
2. Adaptability and Versatility
In this technologically driven era we are currently living in, the world is constantly evolving. From audiences changing their preferences to the emergence of new trends, humans are able to quickly respond to these changes which helps them stay relevant and maintain a strong connection with their followers. They can alter their content based on real time feedback, discuss current issues, and attend live events. All of which make their influence more appealing.
Although AI influencers are capable of creating content and interacting with their audiences, they are programmed, and they can only do what they have been programmed to do. Unlike humans, they can’t act on their instincts and adapt to the nuanced behaviors and preferences of their followers. Additionally, they lack the flexible and spontaneous nature of human interaction.
3. Credibility and Trustworthiness
Influencer marketing has become the hallmark of marketing campaigns. When a successful influencer endorses a brands products or services, they sell out. This is because influencers already have an audience that trusts them, and if they say something is worth spending money on, their audience believes them, and at some point, they will go out and purchase it. An artificial entity does not have this ability. As mentioned, AI influencers have been programmed; therefore, they can’t offer genuine reviews or testimonials. While you can trust the reliability of a machine that constantly delivers, you can’t trust an AI influencer who is controlled by their brands or creators because they are biased, and they will highlight all the positives about their products and services.
4. Human Creativity
Artificial intelligence can create impressive content. AI influencers can draw, make music, write, and participate in many other creative endeavors. But what they don’t have is the innate creativity that comes from the human experience. Human creativity is driven by unique perspectives, emotions, and personal experiences. They tell engaging stories and are constantly coming up with innovative ways to do things. Again, this creative expression cannot be replicated by artificial intelligence.
5. Ethical Considerations
As mentioned, trust is essential when it comes to influencer marketing, and the use of AI influencers makes audiences suspicious about authenticity, transparency, and the possibility of manipulation. Audiences are likely to feel uncomfortable about endorsements that do not come from real people. Furthermore, most brands are not willing to work with AI influencers due to ethical concerns and the potential backlash.
KBV research suggests that the virtual influencer market is set to reach $37.8 billion by 2030. Although it will capture a substantially large portion of the market, artificial intelligence will not replace it. There are many limitations for this to happen; therefore, human influencers should not view AI influencers as a threat to their earning potential, but as an enhancement to it.

title: UiPath CEO Defines Future Of Business Robotics In A World Of ‘Agents’
text:
Robots evolved. From as far back as the early black and white movies (Metropolis) almost exactly 100 years ago, robots finally became real and started to help weld rivets in automotive engineering plants somewhere around the 1970s. They then further evolved into robot-shaped humanoids with Japanese firms innovating proof of concept walking robots, but these have mostly failed to become part of our homes as yet. Then, throughout post-millennial times, software robots or “bots” arrived as the age of robotic process automation started to flourish and our software systems were given new autonomous abilities to perform not just their own maintenance functions, but useful productive business tasks as well.
Notwithstanding that lipservice to our brief history of robots, where we are today with robots and RPA may still be a mix of software and hardware, but first and foremost this is a software-balanced equation.
Bridging The AI Gap
UiPath area vice president for UK&I region John Kelleher is keen to push our notion of robots beyond many of the pre-existing notions of automation.
“We all know about the impact of artificial intelligence. The problem is that there is a gap between the promise of AI and the reality of live deployed environments today,” said Kelleher. “If we look at McKinsey’s analysis of this space, we see that businesses are thinking too narrowly about the business case of how AI is applied at work. As well as technology choice questions, there’s also a key education aspect to overcome and that has to work with data architectures that enables change management to really make an impact in terms of the way IT works with the business function. Aiming to bridge the gap between the promise of AI and real world operational environments, we’re looking at how enterprises can build the operating model of the future to really create a new way of working.”
Today we might think that AI is quite ubiquitous in the sense that it could be potentially applied to any aspect of business. Kelleher says that AI should not be viewed as a single application deployment point in this sense. Instead, it should be regarded as a fabric that can be applied to specifically defined solutions that span an end-to-end operating model across a modern enterprise.
It seems evident that UiPath’s work in the UK and Ireland region reflects and resonates with its work in North America and indeed the rest of the world. As CEO and founder of UiPath, Daniel Dines has more opinions on robotics than most. Talking about what he called the ‘dark ages of AI and RPA’ (and he means as recently as 2016), Dines says that his team had realized early on that both disciplines are symbiotic.
What Is Agentic (Agent-Based) Technology?
“Now that the future of AI and RPA will be agentic, let’s step back and consider what this term means and why it applies to the next age of automation. As a straightforward definition, the term agentic is the ability of an AI system to control and manage the flow of a business process,” explained Dines, speaking to press and analysts in London this month. “Many human actions (such as thinking, moving, blinking etc.) happen automatically without us having to expend cognitive power to make them happen - and I mention this because intelligence in us humans is powered by these automated routines.”
For additional background here, we ourselves can be defined as agents. When a human operative in a call center or a business person at any level performs a function, they can be referred to as an agent. More typically these days we talk about software agents i.e. a piece of software (or complete computer program) that performs a prescribed task for a human user, a machine or some other virtually defined entity that forms a part of a workflow system. So in this context, a human-agent team is a collaborative environment composed of interacting humans working in concert with AI systems.
The clarification is necessary because Dines is painting a picture of a world where human agents now start to increasingly offload their work tasks to AI and RPA. Which aspects of our lives remain our responsibility to execute as opposed to those parts we can give to computers is the next question.
Left Brain - Right Brain Thinking
Dines asks us to think more about automation. He says that if we’re thirsty during the night, we simply get a bottle of water from the fridge and drink. This whole action is automatic, learned and done without thinking, so (as we have discussed before) this is all left brain automatic thinking. Left brain thinking is all about robotics where people create and maintain automation - it’s where structured logical efficiecy-oriented systematic processing happens.
The right brain is all about creative intuitive thinking where we apply adaptability and deal with ambiguity. The right brain is also where we find all large action model autonomous decision making with an ability to manage adaptive behavior.
Being able to bring this element of intelligence into RPA is only possible if we have an AI model that understands exceptions as they happen so that it can learn and navigate real world ambiguities more competently. This is the point where we can add “agentic skills" to RPA and start to channel that intelligence from what UiPath would call self-healing robots into dynamic planning and dynamic learning in business.
Our Agentic Future
“We can imagine AI in the agentic future evolving to a point where it is capable of handling some 80% of what humans do at work. This is where AI starts to take on a more spontaneous (perhaps unstructured and unexpected) role in business (or indeed in applications like healthcare and in any industry vertical,” said UiPath’s Dines. “You might ask yourself what it takes to get to 100% offload to AI agents - I don’t think we’re at that stage with AI today, although we can offload some instances and tasks where this can happen (autonomous cars for example), but this is only in deployment scenarios that have comparatively controlled, defined and safe environments. So we have work to do, but the future is very exciting for sure.”
The company’s comments come at a time when the firm has made some direct updates to its platform. UiPath has now put several new features in its platform designed to infuse generative AI more deeply into the UiPath Business Automation Platform. UiPath Autopilot for developers and testers uses generative AI and natural language processing in UiPath Studio to create workflows, generate expressions and help build automations.
“The new functions include text-to-workflow: developers can simply describe an automation idea in natural language and Autopilot will create the initial workflow. Text-to-expressions: with Autopilot, developers no longer need to remember the exact syntax and structure of expressions. They can describe what they need in natural language and allow AI to generate the correct expression. Text-to-code: generate code from natural language descriptions to shorten time to deployment for automation projects,” noted the company, in a technical product statement.
A preview of the UiPath plugin and integration with Copilot for Microsoft 365 provides an integration that is intended to allow users to automate end-to-end business processes with co-workers directly within Microsoft Teams. Customers will have access to a prebuilt automation library to run automations that complete common, repetitive tasks, along with specialized automations for function- or industry-specific tasks. Users can also discover and run automations their company has developed.
Workers & Agents In Unison
Robotics is on the rise, automations are expanding in their scope, evolving in their adaptability, developing in their capability range and expanding in their applicable surface area in business. With this surge, AI-empowered software agents are now taking on more of our work tasks. That’s not a bad thing it’s a good thing - as one UiPath spokesperson has said, “If you can apply RPA and AI to your role and find a way to completely automate your job, then you’re clearly smart and that’s the most guaranteed way to get promoted.”
However and whatever the outcome of AI agents and RPA automation being applied to business, the changing dynamics here must surely leave management consultants rubbing their hands with glee. If we can automate that (arguably flaky at times) role too, then AI will really have come of age.

title: Council Post: 14 Coaches’ New Offerings In Response To Emerging Trends
text:
In recent years, the business world experienced rapid changes due to technological developments and post-pandemic market adjustments. Consequently, many professional coaches have noticed new patterns in the types of goals their clients are setting and the type of support required to achieve them.
Below, 14 members of Forbes Coaches Council discuss new services and products they have decided to launch in response to emerging trends. Read on for insights into how they updated their offerings and took more flexible, inventive and creative approaches to meet evolving client needs.
1. Revamped Outplacement Services
I’ve introduced outplacement services in response to the uptick in layoffs across the country. Traditional outplacement services are very process-driven and focused on the past, leaving displaced employees stuck in a career path they might want to get out of. My outplacement services are “future-focused” and employee-centric, based on where they want to take their career next. - Franklin Buchanan, Post Up Careers
2. Communication Roadmapping
In a post-Covid business world, one trend is the need to improve teams’ interpersonal and communication skills. Communication styles have a significant impact on team dynamics and organizational effectiveness! My newest offering helps clients create communication roadmaps—written and verbal—that help them build a connection, address conflict and network to get the results they want from others. - Kathleen Shanley, Statice
3. Money Mindset And Financial Literacy Coaching
Job scarcity has contributed to an uptick in female entrepreneurship. But, building from a scarcity mindset means we don’t always consider things such as longevity, impact and generational wealth-building. I now include in my coaching services money mindset and financial literacy coaching, plus access to a custom artificial intelligence tool that helps entrepreneurs of any gender find and access key funding opportunities. - Laura Plato, New Frequency - Coaching and Consulting
4. ‘Coaching Kits’ For Managers
In my leadership workshops, I’m frequently asked how managers can integrate a coaching approach into team meetings to deepen discussions, improve collaboration and spark better solutions. So, this year, we’ve launched a range of “coaching kits,” which contain coaching question cards, worksheets and facilitator guides with instructions on how to run fun and interactive group coaching sessions. - Gabriella Goddard, Brainsparker Ltd
Forbes Coaches Council is an invitation-only community for leading business and career coaches. Do I qualify?
5. Renewed Focus On Retirement
Transition coaching has become a major trend. The tail end of the Baby Boomers is exiting the workforce with strong plans for the next phase of life. Many have entrepreneurial ambitions, and their zest for life shows up in big ways, as they want to plan out their retirement dream. Their investment in thoughtful planning demonstrates they are more than ready to become the CEOs of their own lives. - Carry Metkowski, Carry Metkowski
6. Expanded Options To Invest In Coaching
So many would benefit greatly from coaching; however, they are not able to invest in private, concierge-level coaching. To meet this need, I developed a self-paced program with a live coaching component for my clientele (financial advisors). We also founded a membership-based community with exclusive access to online content, live sessions and group coaching. - Kristin Andree, Andree Group
7. Mental Health Promotion
I remain convinced that performance and well-being can go hand in hand. Facing the increase of stress, pressure and burnout, I have integrated mental health promotion into my leadership development program. Recently, I upgraded it with an AI coach, too. While coaching sessions remain in-person, this program and the AI coach are available 24/7, adding important value to all parties. - Krumma Jónsdóttir, Positive Performances
8. Specific Techniques For Managing Stress
There is a hidden epidemic of stress and neurological issues among leaders globally. Stressed leaders invariably lead to an extremely stressed workforce. I discuss this in my award-winning book and have created an advanced software and technique to easily overcome stress and prevent it from crossing over into chronic stress. This has become integral to my coaching, speaking and workshop offerings. - Dr. Adil Dalal, Pinnacle Process Solutions, Intl., LLC
9. Data-Driven Executive Coaching
A new service we’re offering is data-driven executive coaching. Even though pure coaching is about asking the right questions, clients have less time and more pressure to get better results. Measuring and visualizing the blueprint of their mindset dramatically speeds up learning and their ability to optimize something when they do not know how it works. The more precise and tangible the approach is, the better results they get. - Csaba Toth, ICQ Global
10. New Options For Virtual Sessions
A major trend in the business world has been the decrease in face-to-face meetings. Before the pandemic, I coached exclusively in person. Since the pandemic, the majority of my coaching sessions have been virtual. While I had to develop new coaching skills, I believe it is important to mirror the way leaders meet with their teams. The result is that my availability and effectiveness have increased. - Jill Helmer, Jill Helmer Consulting
11. Big-Business Scaling Tactics For Small Businesses
We coach business owners on how to scale and sell a business. Over the last few years, we have taken the initiative to offer additional services such as lines of credit, merchant processing and software solutions. We took the same approach that other larger ten-figure consulting firms take and brought it to small business owners. - Ryan Stewman, Apex Business Association
12. AI Coaching Support
I coach small business owners, but my impact was limited by the time I have available for one-on-one coaching. As AI and large language models became popular, I developed an AI business coach to support business owners through chat-based conversations. This AI business coach is available 24/7, covers business domains that I don’t specialize in and still provides personalized support. - Minna Hu, AI Business Coach Inc.
13. Mentoring Programs
In response to the demand for development in the changing business landscape, I introduced mentoring programs as a new offering in my coaching services. This trend highlights the value of tailored guidance, especially in multigenerational workplaces. Mentoring helps professionals navigate unique challenges, fostering growth and resilience through diverse experiences and actionable advice. - Martha Jeifetz, MJ - Executive Coaching & Advising
14. Negotiation As A Service
In response to the rise of complex, cross-industry partnerships, I introduced negotiation as a service into my coaching portfolio. NaaS equips my clients with advanced negotiation skills tailored for multi-stakeholder environments, ensuring they can easily navigate intricate deals. When needed, I also sit at the negotiation table on my client’s behalf, providing expert support and guidance. - Alla Adam, Alla Adam Coaching

title: AI: The Supply Chain Leaders’ Build or Buy Software Dilemma
text:
Supply chain leaders love shiny objects. The shiny object syndrome happens when teams focus undue attention on an idea that is new, and trendy yet drop it in its entirety as soon as something new can take its place. Six years ago, the focus was on blockchain. Investments in supply chain using blockchain deployments failed. Tradelens, the largest and most successful supply chain blockchain deployment, discontinued operations in the first quarter of 2023.
Today, the shiny object is Artificial Intelligence (AI). In my recent travels to supply chain events, I find AI discussions everywhere, but the business use cases few and far between. The on AI lack both the grounding in definitions and the delineation of a clear value proposition.
Here I focus on how supply chain leaders can rise above the shiny object syndrome to unleash new levels of value.
The Issue
Today, tension abounds. The most advanced analytics to enable AI are available from the top cloud computing companies of Amazon, Azure, and Google. In the adoption of these more advanced technologies, supply chain leaders face a dilemma.
Manufacturers buy software. They are not builders. The analytics from cloud service providers are best suited for a build strategy. Supply chain leaders saddled with maintenance costs of legacy packaged software are unsure what to do.
As shown in Figure 1, supply chain software innovation is not a normal distribution. In 2000, it was a bell curve with an equal number of early and late adopters. Today, the late adopters outnumber early adopters by a 3:1 factor. So, while many business leaders waft eloquently about shiny objects, they are late followers. As a result, when supply chain leaders speak on “innovation,” they give voice to late adopter perspective.
Figure 1. Software Adoption Cycle
As a result, the packaged software market moves much slower rate than the evolution of tech capabilities. The gap is growing. Is this a problem? Maybe. It depends on the problem being solved.
The Promise
Adoption of concepts like Large Language Models (LLM), Ontological Frameworks, Graph Databases, Vector Databases (Vector DB), NoSQL, and Schema on Read is slow. Existing technologies move structured data efficiently using relational database technologies to improve enterprise transactions, but the processing of unstructured data is an opportunity. Eighty percent of the data surrounding the supply chain is unstructured—text, images, and streaming—but is not used.
The buy strategy assumes that software providers will drive innovation, but it takes time.
The Tension
The answer is not easy. Forms of AI— machine learning, narrow AI, and pattern recognition—are evolving based on schema-on-read databases (relational database structures) using traditional packaged software solution taxonomy definitions, but this approach does not address the larger opportunity.
The problem? Software providers are automating traditional software. Innovation is low. The current focus is to improve transactional efficiency and market insights to improve processes within a function —sales, marketing, R&D, manufacturing, procurement, and transportation. The solutions are inside-out designed to better use enterprise data, but the market is shifting from inside-out process focus to an outside-in business process flow.
The use of unstructured data, in combination with emerging AI techniques, offers great promise to better sense and intelligently respond. The question for business leaders, “Is how to get started?” The conundrum includes:
- Old Tech Is Expensive to Maintain. While packaged software is cheaper for the initial install, it is more expensive over time. Today, based on studies by ASCM, 80% of software purchased is shelfware. (Purchased, but not used.) While the risk of employee turnover and failed projects is lower, maintenance costs (often 15-22% of the initial software purchase) is expensive. The cost of evolving on changing platforms is millions of dollars. (For example, the movement for SAP customers to adopt HANA is a platform change not covered by maintenance.) The question is, “How to maintain and evolve?” The answer is complicated.
- New Tech Is Not for Everything and Everyone. The use of newer technologies cannot be a broad-brushed approach. Avoid generic discussions of AI. Instead, focus on getting clear on definitions, improving capabilities and aligning the AI tactics with business value. The number of resources understanding both the supply chain potential and the promise of newer forms of technology is a constraint. The cloud-based technology providers provide tools, but not process automation.
- Faster and Hands-Free Processing of Existing Technology Is Not the Best Answer. The global supply chain was built on the assumption that demand and supply variability would be low and government policies would be rational. Neither assumption is valid today. As a result, the use of market data is growing in importance. Functional efficiency throws the supply chain out-of-balance reducing organizational effectiveness.
Wrap-up
In summary, side-step the shiny object syndrome. Get clear on definitions and value cases. Align your Information Technology strategy (IT) based on these insights. Delay the investment in major platform investments. Move forward if and only when the organization is clear.

title: Beyond The Gen AI Gold Rush: 3 Guiding Strategic Principles For Marketers
text:
In the Gold Rush of the mid-1800’s, 300,000 people raced to California, pans and pickaxes in hand. A minority got rich from gold – it was both hard work and hit-and-miss. The real money was made by canny merchants like Levi Strauss, who supplied dry goods to the miners and ultimately invented blue jeans. Long-term strategy beat short-term tactics.
Right now, we are in the middle of a new Gold Rush – Artificial Intelligence. And when you look at NVIDIA’s stock price, it’s not unreasonable to call it a gold rush. Like the miners in California, marketers are racing to stake their claim. “There’s gold in them thar AI!” Conferences are so full of AI references that attendees are playing AI buzzword bingo (generated by ChatGPT of course), and even Google installed an AI word counter at its I/O 2024 event.
Having just returned from the Cannes Lions Festival of Creativity, I can attest that AI was omnipresent there too – on the stages and in the award entries. (In fact, while 12% of entries openly sited AI in their cases, many, many more used AI in the background to power their work.) At one of the most well-attended interviews, Elon Musk told WPP* chief Mark Read that, with AI, “this is the most interesting time in all of history.” Big statement.
Moving beyond FOMO, all that hype creates FOMAI – Fear Of Missing AI. But smart marketers are taking more of a strategic approach. What are the long-term wins when the AI dust settles?
